chapters.title: ACT I: PROLOGUE — GALE CRATER COMMISSIONING
chapters.subtitle: Aeolis Mons Footprint, Mars (5.4°S, 137.8°E)
chapters.transmission: SYNOR-1, this is Capcom. Telemetry confirms your pre-deployed cargo hab and ECLSS modules arrived intact at the base of Mount Sharp. Before long-range traversing, you must commission all life-support, power arrays, and radiation shielding nodes. Proceed with EVA protocol.
objectives: Seal interior bulkheads and verify habitat atmospheric integrity
Coupling photovoltaic field arrays to main battery storage bank
Prime O2 water electrolysis stack and CO2 amine scrubbers
Initialize closed-loop graywater distillation and hydro-loop
Command automated regolith berm deposition over emergency storm bunker
Calibrate high-gain dish for Earth uplink synchronization

chapters.title: ACT II: THE ICE BENEATH — ARCADIA PLANITIA
chapters.subtitle: Polygonal Cryo-Terrain (46.7°N, 168.0°W) — 4,180 km Traverse
chapters.transmission: Orbital neutron data from Mars Odyssey indicates substantial subsurface hydrogen deposits across Arcadia's polygonal patterned grounds. Your objective is to quantify ice depth, purity, and ISRU extractability using the LREV robotic suite. Remember: Martian ice is not pure water—watch for perchlorate contaminants.
objectives: Conduct 6x6 subsurface scan using Ground-Penetrating Radar & Spectrometers
Core drill through patterned regolith to extract stratified ice cores
Process sample via Mars Regolith Extraction Unit (MREU) thermal chamber
Determine structural soil bearing capacity for future human landing pads

chapters.title: ACT III: RETURN TO GALE CRATER — UPGRADE & RE-OUTFIT
chapters.subtitle: Gale Crater Base — Ingesting Arcadia Telemetry
chapters.transmission: Spectacular work in Arcadia, SYNOR-1. The perchlorate salt profile you identified has enabled automated synthesis of improved ion-exchange filtration membranes. Overhaul the LREV suspension, inspect the drive motors, and load consumables for the primary science sortie to Jezero Crater.
objectives: Upload Arcadia water dataset to synthesize advanced filtration membranes
Overhaul LREV suspension coils and high-efficiency drive motors
Pack long-duration life-support consumables (O2 bottles, CO2 scrubbers, radiation shielding)

chapters.title: ACT IV: THE ANCIENT LAKE — JEZERO CRATER
chapters.subtitle: River Delta Outcrop (18.38°N, 77.58°E) — 3,790 km Traverse
chapters.transmission: You have arrived at Jezero Delta. Three billion years ago, a massive river breached this rim and laid down fine clay sediments capable of preserving organic biosignatures. Collect high-resolution spectrometry, extract pristine core samples, and establish the regional climate station.
objectives: Laser-scan delta strata and sedimentary fluvial layers
Analyze outcrop mineralogy using Raman and XRF spectrometers
Screen fine mudstones for biosignature candidates & store in sealed cryo-tubes
Deploy automated meteorology and dust monitoring station

chapters.title: ACT V: THE 14-DAY SOLAR CONJUNCTION — THE SILENCE
chapters.subtitle: Jezero Field Shelter — Earth Uplink Interrupted
chapters.transmission: Mars is entering solar conjunction behind the sun. Coronal plasma will blind radio uplinks for the next fourteen days. You are alone, SYNOR-1. Manage power, guard your life-support, balance the sample cryo-freezer, and survive.
objectives: Survive 14 Martian sols under zero Earth communications
Balance power load bus during violent regional dust storms
Maintain cabin O2, CO2 levels below 3,000 ppm, and minimize radiation dose
Safeguard precious Jezero astrobiology cores against cryogenic failure
